clue.text: Family quarrel round vault attracts severe criticism reportedly

parts.note: a dome is a rounded vault forming a roof

indicators.note: reportedly says we want a word that sounds like the slang term for harsh criticism, not its spelling

parts.note: to give someone stick is British slang for criticising them harshly

explanation.surface: A family row that circles some vaulted building draws harsh comments from onlookers.
explanation.walkthrough: In British usage a 'domestic' is a row between people living together, the kind police are called to. STIC is said the same as 'stick', British slang for harsh criticism.
explanation.definitionFit: British police and press call a row between members of a household by this noun, short for a household disturbance.

clue.text: Uncertain remedy to be used under observation

indicators.note: in a down clue, going under means the remedy is written below the observation

parts.note: obs is the standard abbreviation for observation
a cure is a remedy for an illness

explanation.surface: A doubtful treatment that should only be given while the patient is being watched.
explanation.definitionFit: Something vague or little known is uncertain; the adjective covers both unclear and doubtful.

clue.text: Shock! Chosen Republican's old shrewd American

parts.note: elect means chosen, as in the president-elect
R is the abbreviation for Republican; the 's is just a joining 'is' or possessive
in American English cute can mean clever or shrewd

explanation.surface: A startling discovery: the newly elected Republican turns out to be a canny old American.
explanation.definitionFit: To kill or injure with an electric current is to give a lethal jolt, a shock in the literal electrical sense.

clue.text: Thread end of undersheet on to tent, perhaps

indicators.note: in a down clue the sheet's end is placed on top of the next piece
end of points to the final letter of the word undersheet

parts.note: tent is a deep red Spanish wine, used for communion; perhaps marks it as one example

explanation.surface: Camping instructions: pass the cord along the bottom sheet and on to the tent.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Tent' is not canvas here: it is an old name for a dark red wine from Spain. The final letter of 'undersheet' goes on top of it in the down clue.
explanation.definitionFit: Twine is strong string made of twisted strands, so a type of thread or cord.

clue.text: Italian artist drawing on later pieces of Botticelli and reni

indicators.note: later pieces means the back halves of each painter's name are taken, CELLI from the first and NI from the second

explanation.surface: An Italian painter making use of works by two famous predecessors.
explanation.walkthrough: Take the second half of each name: the end of Botticelli and the end of Reni (Guido Reni, a Baroque painter). 'Drawing on' is just a link.
explanation.definitionFit: Benvenuto Cellini was a Florentine goldsmith and sculptor of the Renaissance, famous for his Perseus statue.

clue.text: Rotten move into place that's free

parts.note: to put something is to move it into position
rid means free, as in rid of a nuisance

explanation.surface: Shifting into a spot that costs nothing turns out to be a nasty idea.
explanation.definitionFit: Decaying matter that smells foul is described as rotting or decomposed.

clue.text: One cutting round built-up area merits perhaps three legal points?

indicators.note: round says the cutter's word goes around the built-up area, enclosing it

parts.note: a parer is someone or something that pares, i.e. cuts away
a town is a built-up area

explanation.surface: A cutter working around an urban area earns a few points, perhaps in some legal scoring system.
explanation.walkthrough: The definition leans on the saying 'possession is nine points of the law': someone sharing ownership with two others might claim a third, three points.
explanation.definitionFit: If full possession is worth nine legal points, someone holding a one-third share would deserve three of them.

clue.text: A famous Belgian's got twice this money

indicators.note: twice this says the famous name is the answer written two times, so the answer is the front half

parts.note: Tintin is the boy reporter in Hergé's comic strips, Belgium's best-known fictional hero

explanation.surface: A celebrated Belgian has doubled the sum of money he holds.
explanation.walkthrough: The Belgian is Tintin, Hergé's comic-strip reporter; his name is the answer written twice. 'Got' is a link.
explanation.definitionFit: Tin is old British slang for cash, from the metal coins.

clue.text: Come into mine where pits are getting stripped down

indicators.note: stripped down says each of the three words loses its outer covering, its first and last letters

explanation.surface: A miner's instruction: come down the shaft where the pits are being dismantled.
explanation.walkthrough: Strip the first and last letters from 'mine', 'where' and 'pits' to leave IN, HER and IT. 'Are' is a link.
explanation.definitionFit: To come into money or property is to receive it as an heir after a death.

clue.text: Security police that can have no rotten apples?

definitions.text: Security police that can have no rotten apples?

parts.words: Security police that can have no rotten apples?
parts.note: a section of the British police dealing with national security, read as an unusual bough of an apple tree that bears no bad fruit

explanation.surface: Musing on whether an elite police unit can be free of corrupt officers.
explanation.walkthrough: The British police unit that handles national security is read as a particular bough of a tree; 'rotten apples' plays on the saying about bad apples among officers.
explanation.definitionFit: The Metropolitan Police security unit takes its name from being a distinct division, with a pun on a tree's limb bearing only sound apples.

clue.text: Utterly unusual, but not unknown, sea creature

indicators.note: unusual says the remaining letters are rearranged into a new order
but not tells us to remove the unknown from the word Utterly

parts.note: y is a standard algebraic symbol for an unknown quantity

explanation.surface: A wholly strange creature of the sea, though not one nobody has heard of.
explanation.walkthrough: Take Y (an unknown in algebra) out of UTTERLY, leaving UTTERL, then rearrange those letters.
explanation.definitionFit: Marine shelled reptiles such as the loggerhead are sea creatures.

clue.text: Anger about running conflict and items that might be smelted for weapons

definitions.text: items that might be smelted for weapons

indicators.note: about says the word for anger goes around the other pieces, enclosing them

parts.note: ire is a literary word for anger
on means running, as a machine that is on
a war is a conflict

explanation.surface: Anger at an ongoing war, and at household goods that could be melted down for arms.
explanation.walkthrough: The definition recalls wartime appeals to melt down household pots and pans for munitions.
explanation.definitionFit: Pots, pans and other household goods made of the metal Fe are the sort of thing collected for melting into armaments.

clue.text: Parliament sits with new term after reform

indicators.note: reform here means the letters are re-formed, reshaped into a new order

explanation.surface: The legislature reconvenes for a fresh session once constitutional reform has passed.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Parliament' reads as the institution; the answer is the place-name that stands for it. 'With' is a link, and 'after reform' is the rearranging signal, not a political event.
explanation.definitionFit: The Palace of the same name in London houses the UK legislature, so its name stands for the Houses themselves.

clue.text: Note people bringing in old volume for restoring

parts.note: re is the second note of the sol-fa scale

indicators.note: bringing in says the people's word takes the other letters inside it

parts.note: a nation is a people

explanation.surface: A note to the public about bringing in an old book to be restored.
explanation.definitionFit: Repair and refurbishment of a building is the act of making it as good as new.

clue.text: Designer's skill introducing clubs had an impact on city

indicators.note: introducing says the other pieces are brought inside the word for skill

parts.note: art means skill, as in the art of persuasion
C is the abbreviation for clubs in card games
hit means had an impact on
EC is the postcode area for the City of London

explanation.surface: A designer's flair brings in clubs that make their mark on the city.
explanation.walkthrough: EC (East Central) is the London postal district covering the City, the financial centre. The 's after 'Designer' is 'has', a link.
explanation.definitionFit: Someone who draws up plans for buildings is a professional designer.

clue.text: Locate some rooms when leaving university

indicators.note: leaving says the university letter departs from the set of rooms

parts.note: a suite is a set of rooms, as in a hotel

explanation.surface: Finding a place to live once you have moved out of student halls.
explanation.definitionFit: To locate a building is to position or place it somewhere, as a verb.

clue.text: So this fawn's returned in spring

indicators.note: returned says the letters left over are read backwards
in says the reversed answer sits inside the word for spring once So has taken its place at the front

parts.note: a source is a spring, where a river rises
taken as written: the first two letters of the word for spring

explanation.surface: A young deer comes back in springtime.
explanation.walkthrough: SO followed by the answer written backwards (URCE) makes SOURCE, a spring; 'this' stands for the answer itself.
explanation.definitionFit: Both are pale greyish or yellowish brown colours, close enough to serve as synonyms.

clue.text: City swindler's answer's succeeded

indicators.note: the 's reads as 'is', so the answer is followed in its place by succeeded

parts.note: a cheater is a swindler
S is the abbreviation for succeeded, as in family trees

explanation.surface: A city con man has had his reply accepted.
explanation.walkthrough: In CHEATER, the A (answer) is replaced by S (succeeded); 'answer's succeeded' is read as the answer being supplanted.
explanation.definitionFit: The cathedral city on the River Dee in Cheshire, England, famous for its Roman walls.

clue.text: Make concession and arrive outside concert before it's time to go

indicators.note: outside says the arrival word goes around the other letters

parts.note: to come is to arrive
a prom is a promenade concert, as at the BBC Proms

indicators.note: to go says the time letter must be removed from it's

explanation.surface: Agree to give way and turn up outside the concert before closing time.
explanation.walkthrough: 'it's time to go' looks like a phrase about leaving: in fact T (time) goes from ITS, leaving IS. The Proms are a famous London summer concert series.
explanation.definitionFit: Settling a dispute by each side giving ground is reaching a middle way, a verb for yielding partly.

clue.text: Type of brassica outstanding in wet soil

indicators.note: in says the outstanding word goes inside the wet soil

parts.note: mud is wet soil
star means outstanding, as in a star pupil

explanation.surface: A kind of cabbage-family plant that thrives in waterlogged ground.
explanation.definitionFit: The plant whose seeds give the condiment belongs to the cabbage family, Brassicaceae.

clue.text: What's put up in mounting cries out for varnish

indicators.note: in says the first reversed word sits inside the second
mounting, like going up, means the word for cries is reversed in this down clue

parts.note: calls are cries

indicators.note: put up in a down clue means the word is written upwards, so read backwards

parts.note: eh is an interjection meaning what?

explanation.surface: Someone baffled by shouts while climbing reaches for a protective coating.
explanation.walkthrough: Both 'put up' and 'mounting' signal reversal, natural in a down clue where upward means backwards: the turned 'eh' (HE) sits inside the turned cries word (SLLAC).
explanation.definitionFit: A resin from the lac insect dissolved in alcohol is used as a wood finish, a varnish.

clue.text: Study of heredity might throw up e.g. Incest

indicators.note: throw up suggests the letters are tossed in the air and land in a fresh order

explanation.surface: Research into inheritance might reveal cases of incest.
explanation.definitionFit: The science of how traits pass from parents to offspring through DNA.

clue.text: Fool shows lecturer a set of answers to problems

parts.note: a don is a university lecturer, especially at Oxford or Cambridge

parts.words: a set of answers to problems
parts.note: a key is a list of solutions, as at the back of a textbook

explanation.surface: A dim lecturer gets found out by producing the crib sheet.
explanation.definitionFit: A stupid person is called an ass, the animal, as an insult.

clue.text: Shift residence without notice

indicators.note: without says the notice is taken out of the residence word

parts.note: an address is where you reside
an ad is a notice, an advertisement

explanation.surface: Moving home without telling anyone.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Shift' is not a move here but a loose straight frock.
explanation.definitionFit: A shift is a simple straight frock, a kind of garment for women.

clue.text: Volatile paint meant finding replacement line

parts.note: tempera is a paint made with egg yolk

indicators.note: replacement says the letters of meant are put back in a different order

explanation.surface: An erratic decorator finds the paint meant using a substitute line.
explanation.walkthrough: TEMPERA, then MEANT rearranged to MENTA, then L.
explanation.definitionFit: A moody person prone to sudden outbursts is unpredictable or explosive.

clue.text: Girl I left very angry

indicators.note: left says the letter I departs from the word for girl

parts.note: maid is an old word for a girl

explanation.surface: A girl is livid at being abandoned.
explanation.definitionFit: Being furious is being enraged, informally crazy with rage.

clue.text: Trust editor to cut review

indicators.note: to cut says the editor goes into the review, slicing it open

parts.note: crit is short for criticism, a critical review

explanation.surface: Have faith in the editor to shorten the critique.
explanation.definitionFit: Belief or faith in someone, as in to give someone credence.

clue.text: Divert five hundred vehicles around when trapped by it

parts.note: D is the Roman numeral for five hundred

indicators.note: trapped by says the turned vehicles go inside it
around says the vehicles word is turned back to front

parts.note: carts are vehicles

explanation.surface: Divert five hundred vehicles round the spot where they got stuck.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Five hundred vehicles' looks like a traffic jam, but 'five hundred' is the Roman numeral standing alone. 'Around' turns the vehicles word backwards and 'trapped by' boxes it inside 'it'; 'when' is a link.
explanation.definitionFit: To divert attention is to draw it away or sidetrack it.
